# Findings (generated by build.py)

Data: World Bank WDI / FAO AQUASTAT via open-numbers mirror, commit `1bd7fac42b`. Water series end in 2022.

1. **13 of 22 Arab countries withdraw more freshwater than renews each year** (SDG 6.4.2 water stress above 100%, FAO class "Critical"). Highest: Kuwait 3,850%, United Arab Emirates 1,510%, Saudi Arabia 974%.
   Class counts: No stress: 4, Low: 1, Medium: 3, High: 1, Critical: 13.
2. **Saudi Arabia: water stress 974%** (last changed in 2018). Withdrawals were 23.4 bn m³/year vs 2.4 bn m³ of renewable internal freshwater, i.e. **9.7x** what renews. Withdrawals grew from 16.1 bn m³ in 1992.
3. **Renewable water per person fell in 19 of 20 countries** with data in both 1962 and 2022 (left out: Palestine, Sudan; did not fall: Kuwait: 0 -> 0 m³). The number of these countries below 500 m³ per person ("absolute scarcity") went from 6 to 16. Saudi Arabia went from 916 to 75 m³ per person (92% less), because population grew while renewable resources are fixed. World reference: median country 2,536 m³ per person in 2022 (n=180).
4. **Agriculture uses most of the water**: it is over half of withdrawals in 16 of 21 countries with consistent sector data (median share 76%). Saudi Arabia: agriculture 82%, industry 5%, domestic 13%. Left out because the source shares do not add up to 100%: Palestine (114.6%).
5. **Water productivity** (GDP per m³ withdrawn, constant 2015 US$): Saudi Arabia $36.8/m³ vs $23.2/m³ for the median country in the world in 2022. Highest in the Arab group: Qatar $684/m³.

Data freshness: for 18 of 22 countries the latest water-stress number is a value carried forward from an earlier estimate (see `last_changed_year` in water_stress_latest.csv).
Check: per-person water recomputed from totals and population matches the published series (median relative difference 0.00%).
